purpose: Trifarotene is a prescription cream used to treat acne on the face and trunk (chest and back) in people 9 years and older. It helps clear up pimples, blackheads, and whiteheads. It is applied directly to the skin once a day.
how_it_works: Trifarotene works by targeting specific receptors in your skin called retinoic acid receptors, which help control how skin cells grow and shed. By activating these receptors, it helps keep your pores from getting clogged and reduces inflammation that causes acne. Think of it as helping your skin renew itself in a healthier, cleaner way.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are skin irritation where you apply the cream, including redness, dryness, peeling, burning, or stinging. These effects are usually mild and often get better after the first few weeks of use. Moisturizer can help soothe these symptoms.
warnings: Avoid getting this cream in your eyes, mouth, or inside your nose — it can cause irritation. Your skin will be more sensitive to sunlight while using this medication, so always wear sunscreen and protective clothing when going outside. Do not use this medication if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as retinoids can harm an unborn baby. Talk to your doctor right away if you become pregnant while using it.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer of Aklief cream once a day in the evening to the affected areas of your face and/or trunk. Use a pea-sized amount for the face and a larger amount for the trunk area. Apply it to clean, dry skin and wash your hands after use.
